papers.title: Nonparametric statistical inference for drift vector fields of multi-dimensional diffusions
papers.abstract: The problem of determining a periodic Lipschitz vector field $b=(b_1, \dots, b_d)$ from an observed trajectory of the solution $(X_t: 0 \le t \le T)$ of the multi-dimensional stochastic differential equation \begin{equation*} dX_t = b(X_t)dt + dW_t, \quad t \geq 0, \end{equation*} where $W_t$ is a standard $d$-dimensional Brownian motion, is considered. Convergence rates of a penalised least squares estimator, which equals the maximum a posteriori (MAP) estimate corresponding to a high-dimensional Gaussian product prior, are derived. These results are deduced from corresponding contraction rates for the associated posterior distributions. The rates obtained are optimal up to log-factors in $L^2$-loss in any dimension, and also for supremum norm loss when $d \le 4$. Further, when $d \le 3$, nonparametric Bernstein-von Mises theorems are proved for the posterior distributions of $b$. From this we deduce functional central limit theorems for the implied estimators of the invariant measure $μ_b$. The limiting Gaussian process distributions have a covariance structure that is asymptotically optimal from an information-theoretic point of view.

summary_en.motivation: To infer the drift vector field of a multi-dimensional diffusion process from a single observed trajectory.
summary_en.method: A penalized least squares estimator equivalent to the MAP estimate under a high-dimensional Gaussian product prior is analyzed, with posterior contraction rates derived.
summary_en.result: Optimal convergence rates up to log-factors in L2 loss for any dimension and supremum norm loss for d≤4 are obtained, along with Bernstein-von Mises theorems for d≤3.
summary_en.validation: Theoretical proofs only; no numerical simulations or real data experiments are provided.

papers.title: IGA-based Multi-Index Stochastic Collocation for random PDEs on arbitrary domains
papers.abstract: This paper proposes an extension of the Multi-Index Stochastic Collocation (MISC) method for forward uncertainty quantification (UQ) problems in computational domains of shape other than a square or cube, by exploiting isogeometric analysis (IGA) techniques. Introducing IGA solvers to the MISC algorithm is very natural since they are tensor-based PDE solvers, which are precisely what is required by the MISC machinery. Moreover, the combination-technique formulation of MISC allows the straight-forward reuse of existing implementations of IGA solvers. We present numerical results to showcase the effectiveness of the proposed approach.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该方法通过等几何分析扩展随机配点法，可处理任意形状域上的随机PDE，对生物力学中复杂几何的UQ有潜在迁移价值。
llm.why_not_core: This paper does not address implant design, biomechanics, or surrogate modeling for expensive FEA; it focuses on forward UQ for general PDEs with IGA.

summary_zh.method: 利用等几何分析（IGA）作为张量PDE求解器，集成到MISC框架中。
summary_zh.result: 数值算例展示了该方法在任意形状域上的有效性。
summary_zh.validation: 通过标准数值算例验证精度和效率。

summary_en.motivation: Extend the Multi-Index Stochastic Collocation method to handle forward UQ for random PDEs on domains with arbitrary shapes beyond squares or cubes.
summary_en.method: Integrate isogeometric analysis (IGA) solvers, which are tensor-based and naturally compatible with MISC, into the combination technique formulation.
summary_en.result: Numerical experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed IGA-MISC approach on non-trivial geometries.
summary_en.validation: Validated using standard numerical benchmarks on irregular domains.

papers.title: Lattice nano-ripples revealed in peptide microcrystals by scanning electron nanodiffraction
papers.abstract: Changes in lattice structure across sub-regions of protein crystals are challenging to assess when relying on whole crystal measurements. Because of this difficulty, macromolecular structure determination from protein micro and nano crystals requires assumptions of bulk crystallinity and domain block substructure. To evaluate the fidelity of these assumptions in protein nanocrystals we map lattice structure across micron size areas of cryogenically preserved three-dimensional peptide crystals using a nano-focused electron beam. This approach produces diffraction from as few as 1,500 molecules in a crystal, is sensitive to crystal thickness and three-dimensional lattice orientation. Real-space maps reconstructed from unsupervised classification of diffraction patterns across a crystal reveal regions of crystal order/disorder and three-dimensional lattice reorientation on a 20nm scale. The lattice nano-ripples observed in micron-sized macromolecular crystals provide a direct view of their plasticity. Knowledge of these features is a first step to understanding crystalline macromolecular self-assembly and improving the determination of structures from protein nano and microcrystals from single or serial crystal diffraction.

summary_en.motivation: To evaluate the assumption of bulk crystallinity in protein nanocrystals by mapping lattice structure at nanoscale.
summary_en.method: A nano-focused electron beam was used to obtain diffraction patterns from cryogenically preserved peptide microcrystals, and unsupervised classification reconstructed real-space maps.
summary_en.result: Lattice nano-ripples and three-dimensional reorientation were observed on a 20 nm scale within micron-sized crystals.
summary_en.validation: Validation was performed through classification of diffraction patterns and reconstruction of real-space order/disorder maps.
